title: Uniqlo Set to Be World's Second-Largest Fashion Retailer
paragraphs: Fast Retailing, the Japanese company that owns the clothing brand Uniqlo, appears to be on course to become the world's second-largest apparel retailer, overtaking the Swedish fashion giant H&M.

In October, Fast Retailing reported record results for its business year, which ended in August. Its sales rose 16.6% from the previous year to 3.96 trillion yen, while its net profit jumped 25.3% to a record 542.52 billion yen.

These figures put the company in a strong position to pass H&M, which currently holds second place behind Inditex, the Spanish owner of Zara. H&M's sales have been lower than the previous year's levels through the third quarter of its current business year, although the company has not yet released its full-year results. According to some estimates, Fast Retailing's sales could exceed H&M's by a small margin when converted into euros.

This would not be the first time the two companies have competed so closely. In 2019, Fast Retailing briefly moved ahead of H&M based on exchange rates at the time, but H&M soon regained its position. Some analysts point out that Uniqlo's rise is partly the result of H&M's own difficulties, not only Uniqlo's strength.

Nevertheless, Uniqlo has been expanding rapidly overseas, particularly in Europe and North America. The brand is known for affordable, simple clothing designed to be worn every day, as well as for functional products made with special materials.
Despite its success, Fast Retailing still has a long way to go before it can challenge Inditex for first place. Inditex's total sales are still around twice as large.

Tadashi Yanai, the company's chairman, president and CEO, has set a goal of reaching 10 trillion yen in annual sales. Yanai said that this target is now "within our sights," adding that the company has reached the starting line in the global market and is taking on a major challenge for its next stage of growth.
However, the final ranking will only be confirmed once H&M publishes its full-year figures.
